classification.difficultyReason: A scaffolded cubic analysis combines differentiation, second-derivative classification, an inflection sign check and a complete sketch.

children.label: b
children.prompt: By solving $f'(x)=0$, find the coordinates of any stationary points.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Examine the sign of $f''(1)$ and $f''(-1)$ to determine their nature.

answer.short: Local maximum at $(-1,2)$; local minimum at $(1,-2)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}f''(1)&=6>0\\f''(-1)&=-6<0.\end{aligned}$$
The curve is concave up at $(1,-2)$, so this is a local minimum. It is concave down at $(-1,2)$, so this is a local maximum.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Find the coordinates of the point of inflection. Remember that you must show that the sign of $f''(x)$ changes about this point.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}6x&=0\\x&=0\\f(0)&=0.\end{aligned}$$
For $x<0$, $f''(x)=6x<0$, so the curve is concave down. For $x>0$, $f''(x)=6x>0$, so it is concave up. The concavity changes at $(0,0)$, confirming a point of inflection.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Sketch the graph of $f(x)$, indicating all important features.

answer.short: Cubic through $(-\sqrt3,0)$, $(0,0)$ and $(\sqrt3,0)$, with local maximum $(-1,2)$, local minimum $(1,-2)$ and inflection $(0,0)$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}x^3-3x&=0\\x(x^2-3)&=0\\x&=-\sqrt3,\ 0,\ \sqrt3.\end{aligned}$$
The function is odd, so its graph has rotational symmetry about the origin. Use the stationary points and inflection point found above. The curve increases for $x<-1$ and $x>1$, and decreases for $-1<x<1$. As $x\to-\infty$, $f(x)\to-\infty$; as $x\to\infty$, $f(x)\to\infty$.

spec.description: Equation-driven cubic with arrowed axes, marked turning points and nonzero x-intercepts. The curve passes through the origin. Ordinary axes and labels are black; the function uses standard blue.
spec.mathematics: f(x)=x^3-3x; turning points (-1,2), (1,-2); roots -sqrt(3), 0, sqrt(3); inflection (0,0).
